pages: FastWoe Fast Weight of Evidence Encoding and Inference FastWoe is a predictive modeling toolkit based on weight of evidence (WOE) transformation methods, with theoretical foundations in information theory, now standard in credit scoring With FastWoe you can perform univariate screening, calculate uncertainty of WOE & IV, calculate Somers’ D / Gini, perform inference with Naïve Bayes classification for binary and multiclass problems For binning continuous features, FastWoe offers decision trees, histograms, and FAISS Kmeans (both CPU and GPU modes supported) With recent additions, FastWoe includes new plotting batteries to draw cumulative accuracy profile (CAP) curves and perform efficient variable screening with Marginal Somers’ D (MSD) Other improvements include ultra-fast installs (total package size is under 70 KB!) and supports Python 3.9+ versions 1. GitHub repo: www.github.com/xRiskLab/fastwoe. %pip install fastwoe from fastwoe import FastWoe X_woe = FastWoe().fit_transform(X) http://www.github.com/xRiskLab/fastwoe

from fastwoe.screening import marginal_somersd_selection # Run MSD feature selection result = marginal_somersd_selection( X_train, y_train, X_test=X_test, y_test=y_test, min_msd=0.01, # Minimum MSD threshold max_features=10, # Max features to select correlation_threshold=0.6, # Max Somers’ D ties="y", random_state=42, ) print(f"Features: {result['selected_features']}") FastWoe Marginal Somers’ D Marginal Somers’ D (MSD) selects features by their incremental rank correlation with what the current model does not explain. The first feature maximizes Somers’ D with the target. Each subsequent feature maximizes Somers’ D with the model residuals, subject to a correlation filter. 1. FastWoe Cumulative Accuracy Profile (CAP) Curves Cumulative Accuracy Profile (CAP) is a credit risk data science plotting tool to visualize discriminatory power of the model CAP allows to see the capture rate of defaults at different proportions of the scored population, the area between the model curve and ideal – random is the Accuracy Ratio (Gini, Somers’ D, AUC × 2 – 1) Notebook: https://lnkd.in/d_8MPSmH. from fastwoe.plots import plot_performance fig, ax, ginis = plot_performance( y_true=y_test, y_pred=[ predictions["Logistic"], predictions["Random Forest"], predictions["Gradient Boosting"], ], labels=[ "Logistic", "Random Forest", "Gradient Boosting” ], ) https://lnkd.in/d_8MPSmH

FastWoe Visualization Decorators 1. The @iv_styled decorator automatically applies IV analysis styling to check the variable screening. 2. The @styled decorator allows you to turn any DataFrame into a stylized version for highlighting the relevant points for communicating the results. Notebook: https://lnkd.in/du4dxibN. from fastwoe.display import iv_styled @iv_styled def get_iv_analysis(): """Get IV analysis with automatic styling.""" return woe_encoder.get_iv_analysis() # Automatically returns styled output get_iv_analysis() from fastwoe.display import styled @styled( highlight_cols=["iv", "gini"], precision=4, theme="light" ) def get_top_features_light(n=5): """Get top N features by IV and Gini.""" iv_df = woe.get_iv_analysis() return iv_df.nlargest(n, "iv")[ ["feature", "iv", "gini", "iv_se"] ] # Get Top 5 Features get_top_features_light(n=5) https://lnkd.in/du4dxibN
